transcript.text: microwve plate wont go round anymore, food hot on one side cold on other. still heats tho

If the turntable isn't rotating, your food will cook unevenly because one side gets all the microwave energy. The most common cause is simply that the glass tray hasn't been placed correctly on its drive coupler, or something inside the cabinet is catching it. Please unplug the microwave first for safety. Is the small plastic piece in the centre of the floor (the coupler) cracked or broken?
2. Is the roller ring under the tray clean, and can you see anything inside the cabinet that might be stopping the plate from spinning freely? Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

yeah the plastic bit in the middle has a crack in it and the hole looks kinda rounded. roller ring is in place and the wheels spin fine, nothing stuck under it. i dropped the plate in the sink last week and put it back on a bit rough

Because it has rounded out and cracked from being dropped, it can no longer grip the drive shaft properly to turn the tray. To get you the correct replacement part, I need to know exactly which microwave you have. Could you please check the rating plate or label on your unit (usually inside the door frame or on the back) and tell me the make and model number? Once I have that, I can confirm exactly what part you need.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Sharp, model R272WM, found it on the label at the back

[Heading: Likely cause: turntable coupler]
The cracked and rounded plastic piece in the centre is the turntable coupler. Because it has been damaged by the impact, it can no longer grip the drive shaft to spin your plate, which explains why one side of your food stays cold. I cannot confirm a specific part number for the Sharp R272WM from my database, but this is a standard owner-replaceable item. You will need to buy a replacement coupler (often called a 'turntable spider' or 'drive hub') that matches the three-pronged shape of your existing one. Please unplug the microwave before removing the broken piece and fitting the new one.
